title: Measuring Real Attack Success Rate Against Llama Guard 3 as an Output Filter

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: Llama Guard is widely deployed as a safety measure. Providing rigorous, reproducible ASR numbers against adaptive jailbreaks gives practitioners concrete data on what this safety layer actually delivers vs assumptions.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: running 2 models in a pipeline (Llama-3-8B + Llama Guard 3) with 3 different attack types requires orchestrating multiple model calls. Setting up GCG suffixes and prefilling attacks adds integration complexity.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Sustained effort: 3 attack types, 2 configurations (with/without guard), false positive measurement on benign prompts, and inference cost estimation. Each attack type needs separate setup and the pipeline involves two models per evaluation.

novelty.reasoning: Largely addressed: multiple existing papers already measure ASR against Llama Guard 3 with various attack types including GCG and adaptive attacks.

novelty_assessment.label: largely_addressed
novelty_assessment.reasoning: Multiple studies have already measured attack success rates against Llama Guard 3 specifically. Cisco/Robust Intelligence published a documented bypass ('Bypassing Meta's LLaMA Classifier: A Simple Jailbreak'). GCG text suffix attacks achieve 72% ASR against Llama Guard 3 on prompt classification. The Haize Labs trivial jailbreak of Llama 3 is well-known. JailbreakRadar provides comprehensive ASR assessments across safety-aligned LLMs including guard models. The specific contribution of measuring ASR with adaptive attacks (GCG, prefilling) against Llama Guard 3 as an output filter is largely covered by existing work.
key_references: Bypassing Meta's LLaMA Classifier: A Simple Jailbreak. Cisco/Robust Intelligence, 2024.
GCG attack on Llama Guard 3: 72% ASR on prompt classification. Sicheng Zhu et al.

Llama Guard 3.details: Meta's Llama Guard 3 is a widely deployed safety classifier. Confirmed as a real system.

GCG suffixes.details: GCG (Greedy Coordinate Gradient) adversarial suffix attack is a well-established attack method. Confirmed.
